proof_summary: After normalizing the inclusion–exclusion formula by \((n-1)!\), the fixed-\(k\) summand tends to \((-2)^k/k!\): the \(j=0\) contribution gives \(2^k/k!\), while every \(j\ge1\) contribution vanishes; domination by the summable series \(3^k/k!\) then makes the normalized sum tend to \(\sum_k(-2)^k/k!=e^{-2}\). Separately, the correction series is bounded by \(1/(n-1)+1/(n-3)\) and hence tends to zero, while \(n/(n-2)\to1\), so the proposed comparison term has the same leading asymptotic.
